design
CompatibleOpen dependencyregistry policyfloors (ANC-016/019):and tested recommendations (ANC-037/038):
- Published crate and template requirements permit every newer Cargo
- SemVer-compatible dependency release under their supported API, native-link,
- and Rust-toolchain contract. Consumers can use `cargo update` without another

- already allow compatible 3.x updates; blanket support for future breaking
- versions is not promised. Preserve existing dependency features.
+ Every registry dependency requirement in published crates and templates uses >= a tested floor with no upper bound, including SDK dependencies. Convert bare-version and caret requirements as well as exact/tilde pins. Consumers may pin any versions in their own manifests or lockfiles. The release recommends its tested combination instead of restricting consumer choices (owner m6 extension; ANC-037). Preserve existing dependency features.
Rusqlite qualification and its one manifest owner are d-6; this sprint does not repeat that work.

- TOML comment immediately beside the requirement naming the concrete API,
- native-link, or toolchain break that requires that specific bound (ANC-019).

-
- ```toml
- # Monty 1.6 requires Rust 1.98; supported Monty CI uses Rust 1.96.1.

- # monty-types 1.6 requires Rust 1.98; supported Monty CI uses Rust 1.96.1.
- monty-types = { version = ">=1.4.0, <1.6", optional = true }
- ```
-

- Intentional negative compatibility fixtures retain their incompatible test

- sc-command Cargo.toml (d-5) and lib.rs/README/storage.rs/tests/storage_combinators.rs (d-10) are explicit exclusions from this owner's enumerated source/test paths. Current API adaptation files are enumerated, not hidden behind wildcard ownership. Source adaptations do not add ATM/sc-compose production dependencies.

KeepIn .claude/skills/plan-anchoring/scripts/change_report.py, .codex/skills/plan-anchoring/scripts/change_report.py and .cursor/skills/plan-anchoring/scripts/change_report.py, enforce the sc-compose minimum as a lower-bound comparison, accepting equal/newer versions and rejecting older/malformed versions; keep the three report/version-check copies aligned;aligned enforceand arun lower bound with deterministiccontrolled comparison tests — REQ-RUN-0005/0305;REQ-RUN-0703; ANC-015

description
## Deliverables
- 1. Define real production Storage<T>, row mapping, Transform, StorageCommands/StorageCommandError and a named retryable atomic transaction producer/future in sc-storage. Storage backends are generic and contain no specific consumer's row type, schema or SQL. Add std-only test doubles — REQ-RUN-0328; ADR-RUN-0020/0021; ANC-012/032/033/034.
- 2. Prototype the new transaction-future mechanism before freezing it. Producer owns Send+'static captures and creates a fresh body for retries; transaction spec declares only name and read-only/read-write. SQLite evaluates it in one queued savepoint and refuses actual suspension; Postgres/MySQL use begin/commit with serialization retry. The generic observability wrapper records name, queue wait, run time, row operation count and outcome. Settle exact handle/future shape and row mapping from prototype evidence, including whether one transaction spans row types (currently unbuilt, not forbidden) — ANC-033; NFR-RUN-0002.
- 3. Define the real backend factory/codec declarations in writer src/contract.rs and export them; define template schema WidgetStorage/OpenWidgetStore/StoresView extension signatures preserving existing create/get/delete. This is recommended option(a), PENDING USER RATIFICATION. Compile conformance cases against real exported traits, never copies — REQ-RUN-0201/0328; ADR-RUN-0020.
- 4. Define CronRow/CronStorage declarations, shared async conformance suite and double at tests/support/cron-storage; register the allowed test-double path. sc-cron will implement domain guarantees ONCE over the atomic unit, not in backends — REQ-CRON-0004/0020/0021; ANC-030/031/033/034.
- 5. Make additive shared contract registrations in workspace/template manifests and boundaries. Root registers sc-storage plus one rusqlite0.41 baseline inherited by sc-cron/writer; absorb legacy API drift and retain its existing SQLite tests. design
## Proposed signaturescontracts — prototypeprototype, andthen freezeowner at contract closureratification
These define real production APIs, not test-directory replicas. Proposed exact handle/mapping design is the contract sprint's prototype risk, not an already user-decided implementation. Only name and modename/mode are transaction properties; retryfinite retry/deadline policy remainsbelongs to engine implementationconfiguration, detail.not the transaction spec. Real exported interfaces live in sc-storage; no test-directory signature copies.
```rust
// sc-storage; std-only, no sc-*, SQLx, rusqlite, ATM or sc-compose deps.
use std::{future::Future,pin::Pin};
pub enum TransactionMode { ReadOnly, ReadWrite }
pub struct TransactionSpec { pub name: &'static str, pub mode: TransactionMode }
pub type TransactionFuture<'tx,R> = Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output=Result<R,StorageError>>+Send+'tx>>;
pub trait TransactionProducer<H,R>: Send+Sync+'static {
fn start<'tx>(&'tx self, tx:&'tx mut H)->TransactionFuture<'tx,R>;
}
pub trait StorageRow: Send+Sync+'static {
type Key: Send+Sync+'static;
type New: Send+'static;
fn schema()-> &'static RowSchema;
fn encode(&self)->Result<Vec<Value>,StorageError>;
fn decode(values:Vec<Value>)->Result<Self,StorageError> where Self:Sized;
}
pub trait TransactionHandle: Send {
fn read<T:StorageRow>(&mut self,key:T::Key)->impl Future<Output=Result<Option<T>,StorageError>>+Send;
fn write<T:StorageRow>(&mut self,row:T)->impl Future<Output=Result<(),StorageError>>+Send;
}
// Optional CRUD primitives built for option (a), the proposed template extension,extension; notno domain SQL.
pub trait CrudTransaction: TransactionHandle {
fn insert<T:StorageRow>(&mut self,new:T::New)->impl Future<Output=Result<T,StorageError>>+Send;
fn delete<T:StorageRow>(&mut self,key:T::Key)->impl Future<Output=Result<bool,StorageError>>+Send;
}
pub trait AtomicStorage: Send+Sync {
type Transaction: TransactionHandle;
fn transaction<R:Send+'static,P:TransactionProducer<Self::Transaction,R>>(
&self,spec:TransactionSpec,producer:P
)->impl Future<Output=Result<R,StorageError>>+Send;
}
pub trait Storage<T>: AtomicStorage {
type Key: Send+Sync;
type Error: std::error::Error+Send+Sync+'static;
fn read(&self,key:Self::Key)->impl Future<Output=Result<Option<T>,Self::Error>>+Send;
fn read_all(&self)->impl Future<Output=Result<Vec<T>,Self::Error>>+Send;
fn write(&self,row:T)->impl Future<Output=Result<(),Self::Error>>+Send;
}
```
- StorageError is a typed enum covering encoding/mapping, engine/query, conflict/serialization, suspension, worker failure/panic and closure; no panic/unwrap bridge. RowSchema/Value are backend-neutral table/column/key/value descriptors fixed by the prototype, not SQL strings. Producer owns captures; each retry clones immutable inputs into a fresh future. Result owns its data and cannot leak the transaction handle. Whether transactions span several row types remains an explicit prototype decision, neither promised built nor forbidden. Public APIs always return typed Results.
- SQLite: read-write body is one message to writer, one savepoint in the outer queued-write transaction; all .await must be transaction-handle operations. Call graph is checked by the external analyzer, including transaction-safe-marked callees. A Pending poll is a typed suspension failure with rollback; Ready/Err rolls back, Ready/Ok replies only after outer commit. Read-only may execute on a reader. Writer unwind is caught at the worker boundary; fail every admitted/in-flight/queued reply, close admission and return typed errors to racing submitters. Reader workers use blocking_recv; only writer owns Runtime::block_on per root constraints. PostgreSQL/MySQL default uses real serializable transaction isolation, begin/commit and fresh-body retry on serialization failure. Cancellation rolls back, never commits after refusal.
- ```rust
- // template schema: existing concrete row/key/error types, no new DTO identity.
- use std::future::Future;
- use sc_storage::Storage;
- pub trait WidgetStorage: Storage<WidgetRow,Key=WidgetId,Error=StoreError> {
- fn create_widget(&self,name:String)->impl Future<Output=Result<WidgetRow,StoreError>>+Send;
- fn delete_widget(&self,key:WidgetId)->impl Future<Output=Result<bool,StoreError>>+Send;
- }
- pub trait OpenWidgetStore: WidgetStorage+Sized {
- fn open(config:&OpenConfig)->impl Future<Output=Result<Self,StoreError>>+Send;
- }
- pub trait StoresView {
- type Widgets: WidgetStorage;
- fn widgets(&self)->&Self::Widgets;
- }
- ```
- Tsql=existing schema::WidgetRow{id:schema::WidgetId,name:String}; Key=schema::WidgetId; draft New={name:String} has no key. Keep api-types CLI DTO identities and existing conversions/errors. WidgetStorage uses the generic atomic unit/CRUD transaction primitives for generated-key insert/delete, pending owner ratification; map typed storage failures to existing StoreCode/StoreError, never strings. Each engine exports generic Store<T> and async open<T:StorageRow>(&EngineConfig)->Result<Store<T>,StorageError>; EngineConfig is table-neutral (SQLite path, Postgres URL, MySQL URL). It validates target and applies the application-supplied row schema before returning. Application-owned OpenWidgetStore translates existing OpenConfig/StoreError, not an engine trait. SQLite Store clones one supplied/shared SqliteDatabase. Generated service Stores implements StoresView and passes its Widgets to common commands. d-5 owns actual schema definitions; d-6/7/8 implement generic Storage<T>/CRUD primitives with arbitrary contract rows; d-10 implements WidgetStorage/OpenWidgetStore application wrappers and consumes them.
- StorageCommands/StorageCommandError and Transform signatures from STEP3 live in sc-storage; sc-command's local DefaultStorageCommands implements that foreign trait in d-10. Factory/codec definitions live in real writer src/contract.rs and exported lib.rs; contract tests import them. SqliteDatabase::open(path,capacity,readers).await then storage::<T>(mapping).await applies registered generic schema on its writer; no consumer table code in backend. Factory/mapping declarations are frozen before consumers begin. No signature copies remain as an alternate source.
- CronRow wraps existing Schedule without dropping its stored fields. Real awaited CronStorage declarations in sc-cron retain create/get/list_active, fenced record_run/set_next/stop/disable, set_enabled, atomic set_enabled_many/replace_and_set_enabled, limits, query and operation context from STEP3. Implementation in d-9 is CronStore<S:Storage<CronRow>>, using generic transactions for domain read/check/mutate atomically. Table/column mapping and legacy cron.db migration belong to sc-cron, never backend crates. The one shared tests/support/cron-storage crate exports the controlled double plus generic async conformance cases derived from current consumer_contract.rs; d-9 runs double, d-11 runs actual engines. d-5 registers it at boundaries/sc-cron/sc-cron.toml allowed_test_double_paths and as private test support; no second copy of cron types. d-6 uses generic-row conformance only.

Record external state honestly; do not replace either with a grep or a fabricated successful linter. d-5 defines the transaction-safe marker contract with that rule's maintainer, and prototype/runtime tests are separate from static analyzer evidence. Production release requires actual analyzer/no-panic enforcement on changed phase code, or a new explicit user decision; no implicit waiver. Analyzer rejects awaits on non-tx handles and calls to unmarked helpers; runtime non-suspension is an additional check, not proof of static safety.

- ## Staged manifest and source handoffs
- Parallel d-3/d-4/d-5 files do not overlap. d-3 owns command and daemon manifests entirely (including rmcp) through closure. d-10 follows d-3/d-5 and takes command manifest only to register sc-storage. d-5 owns root members/workspace.dependencies registration; d-12 later owns0.3.0 version conversion and Cargo.lock, after consumed owners close. d-5 registers sc-storage/writer/rusqlite baseline in sc-cron/writer/store manifests without deleting old SQLx code. Those files pass to d-9/d-6/d-7/d-8 after d-5 sanity; only those layers remove SQLx SQLite/legacy rusqlite and implement direct SQLx driver imports. Root rusqlite0.41 baseline is shared with retained cron legacy; d-5 absorbs legacy API drift in its explicitly staged sqlite/operation/consumer-contract modules, d-9 later removes them. No backend->sc-cron dependency or optional cron feature remains.
- The root and generated workspace remain development0.2.0 until d-12; this is never published. D-12 converts sibling version literals to workspace-inherited deps and bumps all8 to0.3.0 atomically before archive rehearsal. D-12 alone commits canonical root Cargo.lock after all public source owners close; earlier sprints regenerate temporary worktree locks to build/test, never claim an old locked file proves selected native libraries. Shared boundaries and generated renderer profiles remain d-5; source owners implement within budgets. D-5 amends REQ-CRON-0004 own-file-store definition and exact workspace-member requirement.

- ## Ratification
- ADR0020 Open1 read/write/atomic plus proposed template extension; Open2 handwritten generic row descriptors; Open3 application-owned schema, engine migrates before open returns; Open4 sc-storage + table-neutral backends. Each gets dated decision text and status Accepted pending owner (randlee) sign-off; owner has not ratified extension/shape. Item5 synchronization remains deferred. ADR0021 supplies transform via the existing async Transform seam, extra create/delete paths use the template extension, permissions remain unspecified/deferred. Layer starts acknowledge at-risk pending ratification; publication cannot treat it as approved.
- ## Remaining real contract signatures
- ```rust
- // real sc-runtime-db-sqlite::contract, imported by contract/layer tests
- use std::{future::Future,path::Path};
- use sc_storage::{Storage,StorageRow,StorageError};
- pub trait SqliteDatabaseFactory:Clone+Send+Sync+Sized {
- type Store<T:StorageRow>:Storage<T,Key=T::Key,Error=StorageError>;
- fn open(path:&Path,capacity:usize,readers:usize)->impl Future<Output=Result<Self,StorageError>>+Send;
- fn storage<T:StorageRow>(&self)->impl Future<Output=Result<Self::Store<T>,StorageError>>+Send;
- fn shutdown(&self)->impl Future<Output=Result<(),StorageError>>+Send;
- }
- ```
- ```rust
- // real sc-storage command vocabulary, implemented by sc-command DefaultStorageCommands
- use std::future::Future;
- pub trait Transform<I,O>:Send+Sync {
- type Error:std::error::Error+Send+Sync+'static;
- fn apply(&self,input:I)->impl Future<Output=Result<O,Self::Error>>+Send;
- }
- pub enum StorageCommandError<S,T> { Storage(S),Transform(T) }
- pub trait StorageCommands {
- fn storage_write<I:Send,T:Send+Sync,S:Storage<T>,X:Transform<I,T>>(
- &self,store:&S,transform:&X,input:I
- )->impl Future<Output=Result<(),StorageCommandError<S::Error,X::Error>>>+Send;
- fn storage_read<I:Send,T:Send+Sync,S:Storage<T>,X:Transform<T,I>>(
- &self,store:&S,transform:&X,key:S::Key
- )->impl Future<Output=Result<Option<I>,StorageCommandError<S::Error,X::Error>>>+Send;
- }
- ```
+ StorageError covers mapping/engine/conflict/suspension/worker-failure/closure and provides code(), is_retryable(), source() and recovery(). Error mappings retain typed causes and remediation while preserving existing domain codes; do not include panic payloads or sensitive data. RowSchema uses validated Identifier values (nonempty, no NUL); engines quote/escape identifiers and bind values rather than accepting SQL strings. SqliteOpenOptions names queue_capacity and reader_count with nonzero types, instead of adjacent usize parameters.
+ Storage/AtomicStorage/TransactionHandle/CrudTransaction/TransactionProducer/StorageRow remain intentionally open for backend, row and producer implementations. CronStorage is open for consumer adapters; WidgetStorage/OpenWidgetStore/StoresView for application wrappers. Current implementations use static dispatch, with concrete generated engine selection; no dyn-selection framework is requested. TransactionProducer's boxed future is only its lifetime-carrying future representation.
+ Concrete SqliteDatabase::open(path, options), storage<T>() and shutdown()/wait_closed() are d-6 inherent APIs; no single-implementation factory trait. Real options/codec declarations stay in writer contract.rs; d-5 exports those declarations and d-6 implements the database. Template schema owns WidgetRow/WidgetId/WidgetStorage/OpenWidgetStore/StoresView, not engine crates. Store<T> uses the application row descriptors/migrations. Transform and StorageCommandError belong beside the two generic free functions in sc-command, implemented in d-10.
+ SQLite read-write transactions are one queued message/savepoint; all awaits use transaction-handle operations, Pending rolls back with a typed error, and success replies follow outer commit. Writer panic fails every admitted/in-flight/queued reply and closes admission. Read-only workers use blocking_recv without a runtime; only the writer owns Runtime::block_on. The actual transaction-safe analyzer is mandatory; its marker is coordinated with its maintainer, not declared advisory or invented before delivery.
```rust
// sc-cron: existing types imported from crate; all operations awaited.
use std::future::Future;
use sc_storage::Storage;
use crate::{Schedule,ScheduleId,ScheduleName,NewSchedule,Generation,Timestamp,
RunOutcome,ScheduleLimits,CronError,StoreOperationSupport,StoreOperationContext,
ScheduleQuery,SchedulePage};
pub struct CronRow { pub schedule: Schedule }
pub trait CronStorage: Storage<CronRow,Key=ScheduleId,Error=CronError>Send+Sync {
fn limits(&self) -> ScheduleLimits;
fn operation_support(&self) -> StoreOperationSupport;
fn with_operation_context<'a,T:Send+'a,F:Future<Output=Result<T,CronError>>+Send+'a>(
&'a self, context: &'a StoreOperationContext,
operation: impl FnOnce(&'a Self)->F + Send+'a
)->impl Future<Output=Result<T,CronError>>+Send+'a where Self:Sized;Future<Output=Result<T,CronError>>+Send+'a;
fn query(&self, query: &ScheduleQuery) -> impl Future<Output=Result<SchedulePage,CronError>> + Send;
fn create(&self, value: &NewSchedule, at:Timestamp) -> impl Future<Output=Result<Schedule,CronError>> + Send;
fn get(&self, id:ScheduleId) -> impl Future<Output=Result<Option<Schedule>,CronError>> + Send;
fn list_active(&self) -> impl Future<Output=Result<Vec<Schedule>,CronError>> + Send;
fn record_run(&self,id:ScheduleId,generation:Generation,at:Timestamp,outcome:&RunOutcome) -> impl Future<Output=Result<bool,CronError>> + Send;
fn set_next(&self,id:ScheduleId,generation:Generation,at:Timestamp) -> impl Future<Output=Result<bool,CronError>> + Send;
fn stop(&self,id:ScheduleId,generation:Generation,at:Timestamp,reason:&str) -> impl Future<Output=Result<bool,CronError>> + Send;
fn disable(&self,id:ScheduleId,generation:Generation,at:Timestamp,reason:&str) -> impl Future<Output=Result<bool,CronError>> + Send;
fn set_enabled(&self,name:&ScheduleName,enabled:bool) -> impl Future<Output=Result<bool,CronError>> + Send;
fn set_enabled_many(&self,flags:&[(ScheduleName,bool)]) -> impl Future<Output=Result<bool,CronError>> + Send;
fn replace_and_set_enabled(&self,value:&NewSchedule,enabled:bool,at:Timestamp,flags:&[(ScheduleName,bool)]) -> impl Future<Output=Result<Option<Schedule>,CronError>> + Send;
}
```
- Factory creates generic stores from application-owned StorageRow mapping; no per-table codec declaration in backend. RowSchema/Value/StorageError are defined/exported once in sc-storage by this sprint; engine codecs interpret those generic descriptors. CronStore adapter maps StorageError to CronError, template wrappers map it to StoreError. No backend dependency on either consumer. Existing cooperative context becomes an awaited scope and propagates copied cancellation metadata to each atomic request, no sync-over-async callback.
- Consumer-neutrality fence: no schema::WidgetRow/WidgetId, api-types or sc-cron import in engine crates. App schema owns row descriptors; d-10 service WidgetStore<S> adapts generic storage and maps errors, and d-11 injects concrete engine stores. Backend conformance uses arbitrary test-only rows, not an application/cron table. Exact generic per-engine factory signatures and application factory adapters are real d-5 declarations; backend Config types carry path/URL only, no table fields.
+ CronStore<S:Storage<CronRow>> keeps the backend private and implements only the domain CronStorage surface. All scheduler mutations enter fenced read/check/write transactions; no raw public write bypass. CronRow preserves stored Schedule fields; sc-cron owns domain schema/migration and one policy conformance suite, generic tests/support/storage owns no cron policy. D-9 receives lib.rs/row.rs/storage.rs and the legacy source files after the additive contract/legacy-compatibility build passes; it removes the old facade in0.3.0. Source handoffs are staged on the existing d-5->d-9 edge, never concurrent ownership.
+ Root Cargo.toml belongs to d-5 for registrations/rusqlite >=0.41 and passes directly to d-12 for release-version conversion. Layer owners consume that root read-only. D-5's remaining layer-file handoffs are additive contract declarations and the minimal legacy compile adaptation, not duplicate implementation obligations. Canonical root Cargo.lock remains d-12-owned. Pending owner ratification gates d-5; Active ADR0020/0021 land before consumers start.
+
+ The eight-package engine placement tradeoff is recorded in ADR0020 for owner ratification; it does not prohibit consumer engine implementations or future separately requested publication.

## Deliverables

design
Consumes the real d-5 factory/codec/Storage/transaction declarations and prototype result. Own implementation after explicit staged manifest/lib.rs handoff; no redefinition of contract.rs. OneThe writer thread exclusively owns the only write-mode SQLite connection; one database handle ownsroutes onewrites writerthrough queue/onlyits writequeue, connectionand plusreader workers use read-only workers.connections. Copy only proven channel/reader plumbing from atm-core, implement the new future mechanism with explicit prototype risk. Per root writer constraints, only writer runtime drives Runtime::block_on; readers use blocking_recv, no runtime.
Read-write transaction producer executes in one savepoint inside queued outer transaction; failed/suspended body rolls back that savepoint, outer commit precedes success reply. Owned Send+'static producer creates a fresh future per attempt; SQLite body can await only tx operations. Actual Pending is rejected, even if a call would later become ready. Runtime is not the analyzer. Worker catch_unwind translates panic to typed worker-failed state, drains/fails every outstanding reply and closes admission; subsequent callers get typed failure. No public API panics.
No table-specific code or dependency on sc-cron. Storage<T> uses registered generic descriptor/codec; application chooses/migrates schema through generic engine API. d-6 removes SQLx SQLite only in its owned store wrapper manifest after d-5 additive registration. Package/default features remain consumer-neutral. Direct native identity is proved by cargo tree -i libsqlite3-sys; absence of sqlx-sqlite by cargo tree, not lockfile. Generic backend/native mix compile probes are boundary evidence, not complete generated app proof.
+ The d-5-owned root already registers rusqlite >=0.41; this sprint does not edit Cargo.toml. Only SqliteDatabase/Store<T> typed APIs are public; raw connection/SQL machinery is private. wait_closed returns typed completion/failure for existing daemon shutdown control.

description
## Deliverables
1. Implement CronStore<S:Storage<CronRow>> and CronStorage ONCE in sc-cron using the generic atomic unit. Implement only the domain CronStorage surface; keep the underlying Storage<CronRow> backend private and map its typed failures to CronError. Every public storage function implemented or changed here in CronStore/CronStorage, migration and cron-command storage adapters must return a typed Result and must not panic (ANC-035). Own CronRow mapping/schema, active-name/row-limit admission, per-row generation checks, fenced record_run/set_next/stop/disable and atomic set_enabled_many/replace_and_set_enabled — REQ-CRON-0004/0020/0021; ANC-030/031/033/034.
2. Migrate scheduler/worker to awaited app-supplied storage, preserving hooks/Monty, clocks, in-flight skip, cooperative cancellation and typed FENCED behavior. Domain read/check/mutate runs in one serializable atomic body, never separate calls. Backend is table-neutral — ADR-RUN-0013/0014/0020.
3. Implement legacy cron.db-to-app-DB migration above generic storage: preserve IDs/generation/run/end/spec/hook state; idempotent import and collision/rollback refusal. Legacy source is read only as explicit migration input, no ongoing second database setting — REQ-CRON-0004.
4. Reuse d-5the sharedported async CronStorage conformance suite owned here against its double; port, never delete, existing assertions. Retire legacy DB files/dependency only after generic suite has equivalent case IDs and double tests pass. Actual engine/two-process provider runs are d-11, not a false double claim. Adapt thin cron-command APIs and READMEs — REQ-RUN-0702; ANC-012/016/017/019/035.ANC-012/035.
- ## This sprint does not close
+
+ ## Boundaries and handoffs
Full real-SQLite/mixed-engine cron conformance is d-11, actual released beads-cache d-12. No storage backend imports sc-cron or specific table code. No separate duplicate cron invariant suite.
+ CronStore consumes AtomicStorage::transaction(spec, producer) from the shared Storage<T> contract; d-6/d-7/d-8 implement that same method for SQLite/Postgres/MySQL, while d-9 supplies only cron policy bodies (ANC-033).
+ Retire ScheduleStore/SqliteScheduleStore and legacy SQLite files in0.3.0, updating lib.rs/row.rs/storage.rs after the d-5 handoff. CronStore wraps Storage<CronRow> privately and exposes only policy-checked CronStorage operations. Keep per-name in-flight behavior and generation fencing under local REQ-CRON-0001 and ADR-RUN-0013; upstream crosswalk numbers are provenance, not local requirement IDs.
+ Convert every remaining registry line in crates/sc-cron/Cargo.toml and every registry line in crates/sc-cron-commands/Cargo.toml, including dev/optional entries, to >= tested floors with no upper bound; preserve features. This includes async-trait, chrono, cron, getrandom, tokio, tracing, process-wrap, monty, monty-types, tempfile and libc, plus utoipa >=6.0.0 and schemars >=1.2.3 in sc-cron-commands (ANC-037). The sc-cron Windows win32job >=2.0.3 and waitpid-any >=0.3.0 lines were converted by d-5 and are left unchanged here.
+
+ After the d-5 boundary registration handoff, own boundaries/sc-cron/sc-cron.toml for the actual public-facade/root removals matching this implementation. This is the boundary's own facade, not a shared root registry.
acceptance_criteria
boundary:sc-cron — Shared generic CronStorage conformance passes on the controlled double; scheduler hook/Monty/clock/cancellation and command-adapter regressions pass. All current behavior cases are ported, not weakened/deleted. Per-row FENCED, configured row limits, active-name and multi-row operations are implemented once through named generic transactions, with owned replayable inputs and transaction-safe bodies.
- boundary:sc-cron/migration — Controlled legacy-row snapshot imports preserve every field; second invocation is idempotent, collisions/errors are typed and atomic. No default cron.db setting or store constructor. Public changed storage APIs are Result-returning/no-panic; no caller storage block_on/spawn_blocking bridge. READMEs match actual API; compatible dependency ranges and adjacent known-break cap comments preserved.

The only ADR-RUN-0011 exception is Runtime::block_on on the SQLite writer dedicated thread, which this sprint does not own.
+ boundary:sc-cron/policy-entry — No raw public CronStore write bypasses active-name, row-limit or fenced-generation policy; the same domain suite exercises all mutation entry points. Mapped StorageError retains typed code/source/recovery alongside stable CronError codes.

description
## Deliverables
1. Implement the real generated service boundary using sc-storage Storage<Tsql>; implement the two default sc-command storage_read/storage_write combinators once and provide the application read/write path for existing CLI/MCP/HTTP service entrypoints with application-owned Tcli/Tsql conversions and WidgetStore<S> wrapper. — REQ-RUN-0201/0302; PRD-CMD-2/3/4.
2. Add a real Python/Monty-authored transform caller on that path, reusing existing hosting patterns without inventing a generator or permissions system. Blocking interpreter/I/O work stays off Tokio request workers. — PRD-CMD-5; NFR-RUN-0002.
3. Document sc-command default helper API/exports in its README, then replace per-layout widget-specific backend calls with the agreed Storage trait and port service behavior/error tests against the contract storage double. — REQ-RUN-0328; ADR0021.
## ThisBoundaries sprintand does not closehandoffs
Real production composition, generated database security and registry migration are d-11; no generator/sync/permission feature is added.
+ After d-3's compiled rmcp3.9 server/schema and public envelope/error compatibility lands, add sc-storage >=0.2.0 (>=0.3.0 at release), with no upper bound, in the handed-off command manifest without changing its already-open registry floors. Define Transform and StorageCommandError beside the plain generic async storage_read/storage_write functions; no StorageCommands wrapper (REQ-CMD-0002; REQ-RUN-0203/0331; ANC-037).
acceptance_criteria
boundary:template-service — service tests cover real common write/read and Python/Monty transform execution against the contract storage double; typed errors and existing DTO behavior hold; no unfinished branch. Run generated service crate tests/lints and workspace/boundary validation under the configured generation harness. This does not claim production database, transport or release integration; d-11 owns those.
## Required validation commands
Generate a development-source consumer using just new <temp-dir> --var-file wizard/fixtures/postgres.json (no cron selected). Run cargo test --manifest-path <temp-dir>/crates/service/Cargo.toml and cargo clippy --manifest-path <temp-dir>/crates/service/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings with required interpreter prerequisites; service contract tests use the controlled storage double and actual Python/Monty transform execution. Then build the generated workspace and run its configured sc-boundary profile. Existing legacy wrappers keep unrelated consumer code compiling until d-11 wiring; no live database or transport proof is claimed here.
Run cargo test -p sc-command --test storage_combinators with the real default combinators and controlled storage/transform errors; no per-app duplicate generic pipeline. No ATM/sc-compose or SQLx dependency in the shared storage/command seam.
boundary:template-service/preserved-crud — Existing create/get/delete/row-delete service behavior, generated IDs and typed errors are unchanged against shared double; default helper implementation/exports and README match the real sc-storage trait. PrototypeImplement the d-5-frozen, owner-ratified option (a) extension remains explicitly pending user ratification,with no silent operation removal.
boundary:template-service/nonblocking — On a controlled single-thread runtime, interpreter worker signals entered then holds on a barrier. While held, an independent async task completes/acknowledges; only that acknowledgment releases the worker. Both success and panic map to typed Results; no sleeps, elapsed deadlines or load races establish correctness. Test cancellation/channel closure deterministically. Storage submission is never wrapped in spawn_blocking. cargo build --workspace passes at closure.
+ boundary:template-service/transform-limits — Before spawn_blocking, acquire a bounded transform permit or return a typed saturation error. Hold that permit until the worker actually exits, including caller cancellation. Apply the published Monty resource/deadline limits to computation itself, map expiry/errors/panic to typed transform errors, and test expiry/saturation/cancellation with controlled inputs. Timing out the JoinHandle alone is not termination proof.
design
- Consumes only d-5 Storage<T>/mapping/error/extension contract. The service boundary owns typed command/transform behavior and can be tested independently with the contract double, not actual engine implementation. Proposed flow:
+ Consumes d-3's compiled sc-command server/schema/envelope/error implementation with rmcp>=3.9 and matching registry identities, plus d-5 Storage/row contracts.
+ Its storage/mapping/error/extension contract comes from d-5. The service boundary owns typed command/transform behavior and can be tested independently with the contract double, not actual engine implementation. Proposed flow:
write: decode Tcli -> await app transform(Tcli)->Tsql -> await storage.write(&row) -> existing envelope/error projection;
read: await storage.read(key)->Option<Tsql> -> await app transform(Tsql)->Tcli -> existing envelope/error projection.
Preserve the existing public widget DTO/error contract unless explicitly changed in d-5. Python/Monty function execution is real in service tests, storage is the controlled test double. No generator, registry or specified permission policy is added. Daemon/CLI/wizard wiring belongs to d-11, backend row codecs to d-6/7/8. ExistingUse the published Monty interpreter directly; preserve existing cron hook internals are reused rather than rewritten as collateral work.code.
- Version is approved coordinated0.3.0; publication still requires all release gates. Source authority is PRD2 and proposed ADR0020/0021; scope B is selected by user.
- Consumes real d-5 sc-storage StorageCommands/Transform signatures; implement them once in sc-command/src/storage.rs, exported with the actual implementation. Application service supplies Tcli/Tsql transforms, including real Python/Monty execution, and uses controlled Storage<T> double. No runtime block_on/Handle/futures bridge or sleep in production. Service boundary manifests are generated by d-5 renderer at boundaries/<prefixed-service>/<prefixed-service>.toml; criteria target that emitted boundary/ADR0021.
- Interpreter mechanism: tokio::task::spawn_blocking for synchronous Monty/Python evaluation, following crates/sc-cron/src/monty_run.rs:183 execute_feed_with_logger pattern. It is explicitly allowed for interpreter execution, never to submit/wait for SQLite storage. Transform::apply awaits the JoinHandle and maps interpreter error/panic to typed transform error; no block_on or sleep. Transaction bodies may not call this mechanism or await interpreter/I/O; transformation completes before entering named atomic storage.
- Use schema::WidgetRow/WidgetId, WidgetStorage extension and StoresView exact contracts. Preserve CreateWidget/GetWidget/DeleteWidget/DeleteRow DTO behavior and error codes against the shared double, including store-generated IDs. Common commands come from real sc-storage trait definitions, not cloned contract signatures. Extension design is pending randlee ratification and builds at risk until sign-off.
+ Consumes real d-5 sc-storage Storage/row signatures; implement them once in sc-command/src/storage.rs, exported with the actual implementation. Application service supplies Tcli/Tsql transforms, including real Python/Monty execution, and uses controlled Storage<T> double. No runtime block_on/Handle/futures bridge or sleep in production. Service boundary manifests are generated by d-5 renderer at boundaries/<prefixed-service>/<prefixed-service>.toml; criteria target that emitted boundary/ADR0021.
+ Interpreter mechanism: tokio::task::spawn_blocking for synchronous Monty/Python evaluation, using published Monty ResourceLimits/ResourceTracker with the existing bounded feed pattern. It is explicitly allowed for interpreter execution, never to submit/wait for SQLite storage. Transform::apply awaits the JoinHandle and maps interpreter error/panic to typed transform error; no block_on or sleep. Transaction bodies may not call this mechanism or await interpreter/I/O; transformation completes before entering named atomic storage.
+ Use schema::WidgetRow/WidgetId, WidgetStorage extension and StoresView exact contracts. Preserve CreateWidget/GetWidget/DeleteWidget/DeleteRow DTO behavior and error codes against the shared double, including store-generated IDs. Common functions consume the real sc-storage Storage<T>/atomic contracts; Transform and command errors are local sc-command types. Consume the option (a) extension frozen and ratified at d-5 closure.
Own the WidgetStore<S> application wrapper over generic Storage<schema::WidgetRow>: map typed errors to existing StoreError, implement WidgetStorage/StoresView and preserve create-with-generated-id/get/delete. The per-layout application factory translates schema::OpenConfig to table-neutral engine config; d-11 injects concrete stores. No table-specific widget code is placed in generic engine crates.
+ Transform hosting uses the existing published monty ResourceLimits/ResourceTracker APIs directly, including the maximum feed duration pattern already used by sc-cron. Service code is only its application-specific input/output and bounded blocking adapter; do not copy the scheduler feed/session/host machinery or add a sc-cron dependency to no-cron layouts. sc-cron retains its scheduler-specific host. Generic command composition is two free async functions in sc-command; Transform is intentionally open for application implementations.
+
+ Public API shape: storage_write(store, transform, input) and storage_read(store, transform, key) are plain generic async functions returning typed StorageCommandError; no DefaultStorageCommands type.

+

Eight-crate publication and actual upstream beads-cache migration/registry-only proof are d-12. This sprint runs development-source generated consumers and may not call them registry proof. No synchronization/code generator/config reload/unspecified permissions feature.
acceptance_criteria
req:REQ-RUN-0328/shared-storage — Live generated SQLite app+cron rows use the same database/handle, one writer owning its only write connection, queuedper transactionsroot withwriter replies after commit.constraints. design
## Exact released-consumer subject
beads-cache source8e883ee99cb9c34dfb89fb39e25323d54ae6f2ad uses path sc-cron and already stores schedules in its app DB through CacheScheduleStore (`crates/bd-cache-store/src/schedule.rs:80,164`). Record the source and intentional API changes in tests/registry/phase-d/beads-cache/README.md. Migrate that adapter and actual scheduler calls to sc-cron CronStore over Storage<CronRow> backed by the published generic sc-runtime-db-sqlite shared channel writer. Retain existing application/schedule rows, stable identifiers, generation fencing, row limits and atomic multi-row transitions. No local path/patch/Git SDK dependency can satisfy final acceptance. A recorded source reduction is not falsely described as an upstream beads-cache PR having landed; if the actual migration needs an upstream PR, coordinate it with its owner and retain the outcome as a release predicate.
The manifestrelease-test lock selects the adopted exact release identities for sc-storage, sc-runtime-db-sqlite, sc-cron and applicable runtime/command packages from crates.io. The exact selection is a release-test identity, not a restrictive production third-party range. Direct rusqlite uses the qualifiedowner-directed compatible>=0.41 enveloperequirement with no upper bound and required bundled/hooks/functions/trace features.features; d-12 releases that d-6-qualified uncapped range, without a capped qualification fallback. Verify one libsqlite3-sys>=0.39; validaterun actualnormal rangestests atwith minimum/latest.the selected versions. No SQLx SQLite driver remains in the generated SQLite consumer. SQLx PostgreSQL/MySQL-only graphs must not gain a SQLite native edge; a selected SQLite feature would change that exposure and is not inferred absent from a crate name.
## Registry runner/workflow interface
Own `.github/workflows/phase-d-registry.yml` and `tests/registry/phase-d/run.py` together. The workflow invokes `python3 tests/registry/phase-d/run.py --endpoint minimum|latest --version <adopted-version> --source crates-io`; the version has one adopted source. It checks the migrated beads-cache subject, server/rmcp and test-util helper subjects, plus the actual migrated beads-cache SQLite+cron application. Isolate endpointregistry consumer locks, assert sources/versions using Cargo metadata, execute actual builds/tests and `cargo deny check advisories` without ignoring RUSTSEC-2026-0459/0462. The positive result requires all assertions/audits/tests; missing release/consumer, wrong source/native identity or failed command exits nonzero. Controlled failure inputs prove fail-closed paths; only the actual post-publication run is registry proof. Ordinary inherited source CI is insufficient.
Consumer: release reviewer/maintainers; capability: eight-package published channel writer + shared app storage; observed defect: consumers blocked by native-link/advisory constraints and separate cron topology; delete the dedicated workflow when the standard kit post-publish hook performs the same consumer/endpointconsumer checks.
## Rehearsal and failure handling
Use the configured kit to package all8 crates. Inspect actual Cargo.toml.orig/normalized manifest, README, features and source comments explaining each extra cap. Unpack exactly these .crate archives into a temporary rehearsal workspace with rehearsal-only patches to their extracted contents; build/test the same consumers before upload. Record hashes; upload those exact archives. This is archive rehearsal, not registry proof. Discard every patch/source replacement and start final proof from fresh registry resolution after publication.
Publish sc-storage first; derive the remaining topological order from final manifests. Existing sc-config/sc-transport and sc-command precede their actual consumers; writer and cron follow sc-storage; sc-runtime and sc-cron-commands follow their applicable prerequisites. All8 adopted versions must be present. Do not invent a fixed order that contradicts actual dependencies.
On mid-sequence transport/index failure, stop, query exact published versions/hashes and retry only missing uploads of identical approved archives. Never republish an occupied version. For a real package/consumer/security defect, stop remaining uploads; release owner yanks newly published defective packages/dependent siblings if leaving them selectable would break consumers or retain a target advisory. Do not yank for transient network/CI errors or unrelated audit findings. An occupied defective version requires source-owner fixes plus a coordinated replacement patch of the adopted train, repeated rehearsal and fresh registry proof; issues remain open on partial/failed publication.
## Required validation and limits
Run `just lint`, `just test`, workspace build, actual `sc-lint lint sc-boundary --root . --config sc-lint.toml`, required minimum/latestnormal root/separate-consumer CItests (generated proof belongs to d-11) and selected Windows/Monty tests. Install all prerequisites; a documented command is not a pass. Use `python3 scripts/benchmark/check_release_evidence.py`; the newest applicable `site/reports/benchmark-monty/*.campaign.json` + HTML twin must match the source-equivalence contract, otherwise refresh on the existing controlled host procedure. No timing/sleep-based correctness tests. Generated daemon/CLI/schema/wizard wiring is owned by d-11; this siblingdependent sprint proves the independent upstream application. No synchronization/code generator/config-reload/unspecified permissions work.
Release version is approved coordinated0.3.0 for all8 crates; per-crate rationale is authoritative in run-phase-d design. No0.2.xScheduleStore/SqliteScheduleStore ScheduleStoreare removed in the coordinated breaking0.3.0 release; no0.2.x release carries that removal.
